$comment: Type-check only (npm run typecheck -> tsc -p tsconfig.json). Source is src/**/*.ts; the shipped lib/ and root client.js are BUILT artifacts produced by tsdown (npm run build) and ARE committed to the repo (they are the market-direct-install load-bearing products — see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and ADR.md); rebuild them with `npm run build` and commit in the SAME commit as the src that produced them — the build-gate / freshness gate forbids shipping src changes without a matching rebuild. Do not hand-edit the built output. checkJs:false means a .js/.mjs input is checked only where a top-level '// @ts-check' opts it in (test/, tsdown.config.mjs); outside this scope such a pragma is inert, so add it when adding a JS helper that should be checked. The .ts sources are always checked. strict:true is the project-wide baseline (NOT strict:false); the backlog is about narrowing casts, not loosening the flag. noImplicitAny:false is a deliberate trade-off (this project ships no ESLint; tsc plus the test/build gates are the substitute), so untyped signatures in the host glue stay greppable and never block the build — keep it false unless a module is being tightened on purpose. erasableSyntaxOnly is TRUE (added in ab37724 alongside verbatimModuleSyntax, where it was flipped on because it cost 0 errors — the rationale was not written down then, so it is recorded here): the suite runs on bare `node` (test/run.mjs -> node test/*.test.mjs) with no bundler, no loader and no dependencies, importing `src/host/*.ts` directly (no count is stated here by design: the figure drifted 53 -> 58 as suites grew, and COUNT_GUARD only scans docs plus .ts/.mjs, so a number inside this file would have nothing to catch it), so Node's strip-only loader is the real compiler for every module a test can reach. Strip-only mode cannot execute `enum`, `namespace`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`) or angle-bracket assertions (`<T>expr`) — it fails at RUNTIME with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX — while plain tsc accepts all four, so without this flag a `.ts` file can typecheck clean and only explode when a suite imports it. The flag moves that to a compile-time error (TS1294). Do not drop it while the tests import sources directly; it is not a style preference and it is not about .tsx (this project has none). noFallthroughCasesInSwitch and noImplicitReturns are TRUE as well (added 2026-10-20): each costs 0 diagnostics on this tree (measured: tsc -p tsconfig.json --noFallthroughCasesInSwitch --noImplicitReturns --noEmit -> exit 0) and each catches a real defect shape (TS7029 fallthrough, TS2366 missing return). Neither is implied by `strict` — `tsc --showConfig -p tsconfig.json` expands strict to 9 flags (alwaysStrict, noImplicitThis, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, strictPropertyInitialization, strictBuiltinIteratorReturn, strictNullChecks, useUnknownInCatchVariables, noImplicitAny) and these two are NOT among them, so writing them is the only way to get them. A PITFALLS entry once claimed strict already implied them; that claim was wrong, so test/tsc-gate.mjs now asserts the effective config instead of the prose (the gate, not the comment, is the authority).
